fields.meta_title: Hotel Booking Form for Inns and Room Blocks | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a hotel booking form that checks every night against rooms left and holds group blocks to the cutoff, with requests in your own database.
fields.h1: Build a Hotel Booking Form for Inns and Group Room Blocks
fields.hero_description: List your rooms and your stay rules. Emergent builds a hotel booking form that checks a whole stay against the rooms left and saves each request to your own table.
fields.features_heading: What a Room Request Has to Get Right
fields.features_subheading: Rooms sell one night at a time. These six parts keep each request in step with the room count and the deposit behind it.
fields.feature_1:
Rooms counted night by night

Check every night of a requested stay against the rooms left of that type. When one night is sold out, the form names it and offers the nearest dates with a room open.
fields.feature_2:
Minimum stays by date

Set a two-night minimum on weekends and three nights over a festival week. A request that falls short sees the stays that qualify, not an error message with no way forward.
fields.feature_3:
A deposit before the hold

Take the first night or the whole stay through Stripe or any processor with an API. A request becomes a confirmed booking only after the deposit for that stay is paid in full.
fields.feature_4:
Group links with their own rate

Give a wedding or a conference its own link, room count and nightly rate. Guests on it see only the group's dates, and the whole block closes on the cutoff day you pick.
fields.feature_5:
Arrival notes for the desk

Ask for arrival time and bed type, plus a crib or any accessibility need. Answers land on the guest's record, and the desk gets a list of tomorrow's arrivals each evening.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your code

Publish the form on the property's own domain or embed it in the site you run now. Export the full code to GitHub when a developer wants requests inside a larger system.
fields.why_title: Why Build Hotel Booking Forms With Emergent?
fields.why_description: Galleries stop at the fields and PDFs come back by email. Emergent also builds the room count and group cutoffs behind them.

fields.tab_content_1:
No Saturday without Friday or Sunday

Larkspur House has six rooms and sells Saturday night only as part of a two-night stay. A guest who asks for Saturday alone is offered Friday and Saturday, with 2 rooms left, or Saturday and Sunday, with 4. The guest picks one, and the request lands in the innkeeper's table with both nights attached.
fields.tab_content_2:
A dog room shows only when it is open every night

Three of the 20 rooms at the Pinecrest Inn take dogs. The dog option appears on a request only when one of those three is free on every night of the stay. A guest asking for three nights with a dog is offered Room 12, the one dog room open all three nights, at $517 including the $40 pet fee.
fields.tab_content_3:
Any wedding room unclaimed by day 30 returns

Dana and Theo set aside 20 rooms at the Saltgrass Hotel at $189 a night. Guests book from the couple's link with the wedding dates filled in. At 30 days before the wedding, the block closes with 14 rooms booked and the 6 nobody claimed go back. Late guests see the front desk number.
fields.tab_content_4:
Request 81 keeps its rate at the overflow hotel

The Northwind Water Summit booked 80 rooms at the Riverside Hotel and 40 at the Ferrow Inn across the street, both at $164 a night. Once all 80 Riverside rooms are taken, request 81 is placed in the Ferrow Inn block with its dates and rate unchanged, and #summit-housing in Slack gets a note.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Hotel Booking Form
fields.howto_description: Start from the rooms and what each night allows. The form only asks what those rules need to know.
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every room by type and how many guests it sleeps, such as four queens and two kings with a sofa bed. Requests are checked against this count. A room listed twice gets sold twice. Mark which rooms take dogs or have step-free access.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Note the minimum nights for weekends and holidays, the days guests may arrive, and any dates the property closes. Decide what a guest sees when a request breaks a rule: the nearest stay that qualifies, or a note asking them to call.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick the deposit, whether the first night or a fixed amount, and how long an unpaid request keeps its room. Write the cancellation terms in plain words, since they go into the confirmation email and the guest will read them before paying.
fields.howto_step_4_des: For a wedding or a conference, write down the rooms held, the nightly rate, the dates and the cutoff. Say what happens at the cutoff, and where requests go once the block is full, such as a second hotel nearby.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the room list and the rules into the prompt, with group blocks last. Emergent builds the form and the room table, plus the confirmation emails. Ask for changes in plain English, such as moving the wedding cutoff to 21 days.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Request a stay under a made-up name with a Stripe test card, then read the confirmation on a phone. Try the requests that trip small properties: Saturday alone, the last room of a type, a dog on a night the dog rooms are full.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Put the link where guests look
fields.howto_step_7_des: Add the form behind the Book button on the property's site and in replies to email inquiries. Send each group its own link for the wedding website or the attendee confirmation, and watch which nights fill first.

plan.angle: The Semrush top 10 is template galleries (Jotform, Cognito Forms, Fluent Forms, Neartail, Template.net, Makeform) and conference PDFs from ITU and CILTSA; the live SERP adds a Wix hotel theme, WordPress booking themes and more conference PDFs (IASTED, a Qatar expo) that attendees print and return to the hotel by email or fax. None of them knows how many rooms are left. This page is for the properties and planners a booking engine is too big for: a six-room B&B with a two-night weekend minimum, an inn with only three dog-friendly rooms, a wedding couple's block that returns to the hotel at the cutoff, and a summit that fills one hotel and sends the next attendee to a second. Each tab shows the rule working against the room count in a database the property owns. Generic deposits and slot holds stay on the booking form sibling; the FAQ answers the traveler PAA briefly from the property's side of the desk.

A water-industry summit fills its 80-room block at the main hotel, and the 81st attendee's request goes to the 40-room overflow block across the street with the same dates and rate.
